page: Amazon Web Services i4g.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 16-core AWS Graviton2 processor using the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each virtual CPU maps directly to a dedicated physical core with one thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. The configuration provides 128 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, a 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and a bundled 3750 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark testing highlights solid multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread capacity. The instance recorded 24287.8 on stress-ng multi-core and 8598.0 on Geekbench multi-core, while single-core Geekbench reached 976.0 and single-thread gzip compression settled at 20.32 GB/sec. Memory operations show robust local read bandwidth up to 947.29 GB/sec in cache, supporting high-throughput workloads like Redis SET operations at 18.83 million operations per second and static web throughput of 18.67 GB/sec. Machine learning inference scores are limited due to modest single-core execution and the absence of specialized matrix acceleration hardware.

The Graviton2 architecture presents strong qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out architectures, delivering dense compute and direct-attached NVMe storage with low per-core overhead. The principal architectural tradeoff involves lower single-threaded frequency and non-x86 instruction sets, which may require recompilation or limit compatibility with legacy software. The combination of 3750 GB NVMe storage, dedicated core scheduling, and a high memory capacity makes this instance well suited for NoSQL databases, transactional storage systems, distributed search indexes, and caching tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 16-core AWS Graviton2 processor built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 16 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core ratio, 128 GB of RAM, and a bundled 3750 GB local NVMe SSD. It includes 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In benchmark suites, the server shows stable multi-threaded execution, reaching 24287.8 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 10352.38 in PassMark database operations, and 18.83 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core execution and LLM inference speeds are modest. The combination of dense local NVMe storage and an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio makes this server suitable for high-throughput databases, search clusters, and real-time caching tiers.
